paper.title_en: Scaling laws for quantum reflection of hydrogen isotopes on silicon
paper.abstract_en: Quantum reflection is a counter-intuitive process occurring when an atom is reflected by a rapidly-varying attraction towards a surface, for example the Casimir-Polder force. The reflection probability depends on the attractive potential and on the mass of the atom. For hydrogen isotopes, the potentials are nearly identical whereas significant differences in quantum reflection come from the effect of atomic mass. We calculate the quantum reflection probability for the three isotopes H, D or T falling onto the plane surface of an intrinsic silicon bulk. We show that the results obey scaling laws determined by scattering lengths calculated from theory. Moreover the scattering lengths also obey scaling laws with respect to atomic masses of the isotopes.
